docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: • The Dorm Room Relaxing Light, a system designed to create a comfortable lighting environment by combining user controls with environmental sensing. Although each subsystem performs a different task, they all use a Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano microcontroller and communicate through connectors to operate as one complete system. The first subsystem focuses on user interaction and system control. It includes an LED array, several buttons, and indication LEDs. The indication LEDs provide information to the user while the buttons allow the user to change or control system settings. The microcontroller uses PWM to control the LEDs, allowing their brightness or lighting behavior to be adjusted. The second subsystem focuses on temperature sensing. A temperature sensor measures the surrounding temperature and sends its signal through an operational amplifier before reaching the microcontroller's analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The microcontroller can then interpret the temperature data and use it as part of the lighting system's control. The third subsystem focuses on ambient light sensing. A light sensor detects the amount of light in the room and sends the signal through an operational amplifier to the ADC. This allows the system to determine the surrounding light level and potentially adjust the LEDs accordingly. Overall, the three subsystems have distinct purposes: user control, temperature measurement, and light measurement. Working together, they allow the relaxing light to respond to both the user's inputs and the surrounding environment, creating a more adaptable and personalized lighting system

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text:
• The Dohicky has three PCB boards that communicate with one another. This board in particular has the LED outputs and user interface push buttons.
  • The board has 1 LED for troubleshooting and on/off status.
  • It has 2 LEDs to display temperature information. When no LEDs are lit the temperature is below 0C. When one is lit the temperature is above 0C. When 2 LEDs are lit the temperature is above 100C.
  • The board also has an array of red, green, and blue LEDs that will provide mood lighting. The lighting output is based on the brightness of the room and the user selected mode.
  • For a more detailed system overview see the team page. team 207 report.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The block diagram shows the Microchip PIC-Nano board and its associated inputs and outputs. The general purpose of this design is to receive digital values from its companion boards. The values received will be used in conjunction with user selected settings to perform a set of functions. Those functions include mood lighting and an led light to display information from a temperature sensor. The board runs on 5V DC. The LED array uses a 9v DC bus and is switched on using MOSFETs controlled by PWM modules from the PIC Nano. The device has 3 push buttons that provide digital inputs to the board, which in turn provide the user with an interface to operate the device.

docs.title: Control LED Array
docs.text: Solution Description Pros Cons SN74HC595  Option 1: SNx4HC595 — $1.83 each Can turn on each LED individually. Can control a larger array of LEDs. Limited LED power available. Must be used with other components to meet design needs. MOSFET 2N7000  Option 2: 2N7000 MOSFETs — $1.09 each Fewer components means less error prone. Very reliable product. Easy to design and implement. Less control over individual LEDs. Selection MOSFET 2N7000 Rationale Individual MOSFETs will allow the control of a string of LEDs and are rated for the current and voltages needed. The PIC has enough control outputs that the register is unnecessary and overly complicated.

docs.title: LED Array
docs.text: Solution Description Pros Cons C5SMF-RJF-CT0W0BB2  Option 1: C5SMF-RJF-CT0W0BB2 — $0.21 each Correct form and specs for application. Red can simulate the sunrise/sunset desired for the design. Fairly reliable product that is readily available. Single LED color selection will not provide enough for the ambient lighting design. Low lumen output. C5SMF-GJE-CX14Q7T2  Option 2: C5SMF-GJE-CX14Q7T2 — $0.36 each Correct form and specs for application. Can help create a calming earth-tone mood lighting as designed. Single LED color selection will not provide enough for the ambient lighting design. Voltage needed is slightly higher than other options. C5SMF-BJF-CR0U0351  Option 3: C5SMF-BJF-CR0U0351 — $0.23 each Correct form and specs for application. Blue light can create an underwater or blue-sky effect when indoors. Single LED color selection will not provide enough for the ambient lighting design. Lumen output is low. Selection All three LEDs will be used Rationale Each LED will provide a different color. This will allow for more customization of the resulting color output instead of having only a single color.

External Clock Module

Solution Pros Cons Option 1. XC1259TR-ND surface mount crystal$1/eachlink to product * Inexpensive[^1]* Compatible with PSoC* Meets surface mount constraint of project * Requires external components and support circuitry for interface* Needs special PCB layout. * Option 2. * CTX936TR-ND surface mount oscillator * $1/each * Link to product * Outputs a square wave * Stable over operating temperature * Direct interface with PSoC (no external circuitry required) range * More expensive * Slow shipping speed

Choice: Option 2: CTX936TR-ND surface mount oscillator

Rationale: A clock oscillator is easier to work with because it requires no external circuitry in order to interface with the PSoC. This is particularly important because we are not sure of the electrical characteristics of the PCB, which could affect the oscillation of a crystal. While the shipping speed is slow, according to the website if we order this week it will arrive within 3 weeks.
